text:
pranav: heads-up — ran a quick smoke comparing bitsandbytes weight-only (bnb/llm.int8) vs llm.int8 from the repo on voyager-13b. seeing consistent throughput wins but a small quality delta on longform summarization. sharing numbers and ask for quick triage.

anya: can you paste the exact commands/config? also which tokenizer & prompt set?

pranav: repro snippet below (run on a single p4d):
```
python run_eval.py --model-path /models/voyager13b --quantize bitsandbytes --bnb-8bit-mode llm.int8 --calib-size 512 --eval-set longform-summ --batch 4 --max-new-tokens 512
```
Baseline FP16 rouge-1: 43.2
bnb-llm.int8 rouge-1: 41.1 (-2.1)
llm.int8 (our impl) rouge-1: 42.5 (-0.7)
Tokens/sec: FP16 210 -> bnb-int8 320 -> llm.int8 300

matt: hmm the bnb drop is larger than i'd expect. did you use the same calibration checkpoint seeds? bnb historically uses per-channel scaling + activation fudge.

pranav: same seed, same calib set (we used a small curated 512 examples from news+wiki). no other changes.

anya: quick thought — are you hitting KV cache evictions / dense attention fallback for longcontext? that can change activation statistics and make weight-only more brittle. what was context length distribution?

pranav: eval prompts avg context 2200 tokens (range up to 6k). we did enable sliding-window prefix caching in the runtime.

sophia: ran the same config but toggled cache off:
```
# runtime flag
--kv-cache-enabled false
```
Result: bnb-llm.int8 rouge-1: 41.9 (improved slightly), llm.int8: 42.6. so cache interaction probably part of it. latency also increased ~10% when cache off.

pranav: got a sample diff from a failing case — output truncation / repetitive clause in bnb-int8:
```
FP16: "In summary, the company expanded its product line ..."
BNB-INT8: "In summary, the company expanded its product line. In summary, the company expanded its product line."
```

matt: that looks like softmax / logits scale drift. can you share logits histograms for early vs late tokens? maybe group-size or quant granularity mismatch.

pranav: attaching quick logs: average logits stddev (baseline/ bnb): 1.9 / 1.4  (early tokens), 2.1 / 1.2 (late tokens). so bnb is compressing dynamic range.

anya: two-pronged repro plan: 1) run per-channel calibration (if bnb supports it) or increase calib-size to 2k, 2) try bias-correction / outlier clipping in quant step. Also test with our llm.int8 settings: group-size 128 vs 256 vs 512.

pranav: scheduled quick sweep: group-size [64,128,256,512], calib-size [512,2048], with/without kv-cache. kicking off now, ETA ~45m.

eval-bot: automated eval finished for sweep candidate #3 (group=128, calib=2048, kv-cache=true):
ROUGE-1: 42.9
Latency tokens/sec: 305
Notes: reduced repetition vs baseline bnb but still ~0.3 lower than FP16 on long prompts.

sophia: FYI ran a micro-ablation where we applied a small logits rescale multiplier 1.05 before softmax when using bnb-int8 — topicality improved and repetition decreased on a handful of cases. not a principled fix but suggests scale mismatch.

matt: good clue. could be that bnb uses a symmetric quant clip that reduces positive tail. try asymmetric zero-point or per-channel bias correction (see AWQ paper section 3.2).

pranav: note for ops: if we ship bnb-int8 for hosted, need to add a canary flag that forces kv-cache=false for longform routes until we have a fix. canary config below:
```
route: /generate/long
policy:
  quant: bnb-int8
  overrides:
    kv_cache: false
    max_context: 4096
```

deploy-bot: canary created: env=staging, rate=5% -> route /generate/long using bnb-int8 + kv-cache=false. will monitor errors/latency. :white_check_mark:

anya: next experiments I want to run (assign):
- Increase calib dataset diversity (pranav)
- Try AWQ-style per-channel MSE minimization (matt)
- Add logits-rescale ablation and measure on heldout (sophia)

pranav: taking calib dataset and running a 10k-ish sweep, will post results here.

matt: i'll prototype per-channel bias correction in the quantizer this afternoon. if it helps we can make it an optional post-quant pass.

sophia: can someone add a small eval slice focused on repetition modes + factuality? will help us not chase rouge alone.

pranav: good call — adding repetition/factuality slices now. will update when sweep finishes. thanks all. :coffee:
